The Chancellor of Dominion University, Ibadan, Oyo State, Taiwo Adelakun, has urged graduating students to shun corruption, uphold integrity and use their education to contribute to the development of Nigeria. Adelakun gave the charge on Saturday during the university’s fourth convocation ceremony, where 140 students graduated, including 27 who bagged First Class degrees, at the institution’s premises in Ibadan, the state capital. Addressing the graduands, the chancellor urged them to remain disciplined, hardworking and committed to godly values, warning them against conduct that could undermine their character and tarnish their reputations. He said, “You must become the answer to Nigeria’s prayer and not a prayer point as the problem of the nation. Resist corruption, maintain high moral standards and demonstrate integrity in your personal and professional lives. “Shun corruption in all its forms and never allow the pursuit of wealth, power or position to compromise your integrity. Uphold integrity and use your education to contribute to Nigeria’s development.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The chancellor also highlighted the university’s development over its seven years of operation, saying all its academic programmes had received full accreditation, while three were due for reaccreditation in 2026. He noted that the graduating class, known as the Daystars, was the last in the university’s original sequence of graduating sets, following the Pacesetters, Lightbearers and Eagles. The Acting Vice-Chancellor of the institution, Jonah Akoun, said the university offered 16 academic programmes across its faculties and had a student population of 780 at the end of the 2025/2026 academic session. Akoun said the university was committed to providing an environment that supported learning, research and students’ personal development. “We are committed to building an institution where academic excellence, ethical conduct and personal development go hand in hand.” The Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of the Governing Council, Dolapo Adelakun, congratulated the graduates and commended their parents, guardians and university staff for their contributions to the students’ achievements. He urged the graduands to remain resilient, uphold integrity and apply the knowledge acquired at the university to address societal challenges. The overall best graduating student, Nadia Rita Bayakly, of the Department of Mass Communication, recorded a perfect Cumulative Grade Point Average of 5.0 out of 5.0. The university graduated 148 students in 2024 and 130 in 2025 before presenting 140 graduands at its 2026 convocation. Ademola Adegbite
